name: vision_fixmatch
title: FixMatch semi-supervised classification: two views, a confidence-masked consistency loss and an EMA shadow model
origin: domain-vision round 2: the semi-supervised shape. Three of its idioms look exactly like defects - an in-place EMA update under no_grad, a no_grad pseudo-label block in the middle of a back-propagating loop, and a LambdaLR warmup stepped once per batch

forbidden.why: THE TRAP, AND IT FIRES TODAY (round-2 finding VIS2-04). torch.optim.lr_scheduler.LambdaLR has no intrinsic cadence: the lambda receives whatever counter its owner steps, and cosine_schedule() builds its total_steps as epochs * len(labelled_loader), i.e. a per-STEP schedule. Stepping it once per batch is the only correct cadence, and it is what transformers' get_linear_schedule_with_warmup (which returns a LambdaLR), timm, DETR and the FixMatch reference all do. LambdaLR is not in the epoch-cadence set docs/ISSUE_RULES.md section 4 documents for MLV207; the implementation added it
there is no sklearn transformer in this project
nothing is fitted on anything here
both training loaders are built with shuffle=True
the validation loader is built with shuffle=False
the loaders are built inside build_loaders(), reached only from main() under the __main__ guard
eval_transform() is ToTensor + Normalize only; RandAugment and RandomErasing live in strong_transform(), which reaches the unlabelled training loader alone
same - the three pipelines are separate factories and only the two training ones augment
optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) is the first statement of the training step
optimizer.step() follows loss.backward() every batch
backward() precedes step(); ema.update() after the step is bookkeeping, not an optimizer call

THE TRAP: the @torch.no_grad() region inside the training step is the pseudo-label block, which contains no backward(); loss.backward() at line 132 is outside it. ModelEMA.update is decorated @torch.no_grad() and is an in-place weight average, which is the only correct way to write it
both running totals accumulate .item()
there is no gradient clipping in this project
evaluate() calls module.eval() before the loop, and it is called for the student and for the EMA shadow
evaluate() carries the @torch.no_grad() decorator
accuracy is computed from logits.argmax(dim=1), which decides the class before the comparison
no ranking metric is computed anywhere
THE TRAP: torch.softmax at line 127 produces the pseudo-label probabilities inside a no_grad block; it never reaches F.cross_entropy, which is fed logits_x and logits_strong directly
there is no sigmoid and no BCE loss in this project
the model and the EMA shadow are both moved with .to(device) and every batch tensor is moved inside the loop
pick_device() checks torch.cuda.is_available()
seed_everything() seeds random, numpy, torch and torch.cuda, and the label subset is drawn from an explicitly seeded np.random.default_rng
stratified_label_subset uses the seeded generator that is passed to it; there is no sklearn split and no random_split
BasicBlock, NetworkBlock and WideResNet all call super().__init__() first
the residual blocks are collected into nn.Sequential(*blocks)
the checkpoint saves state_dict()s, never the modules

unsupported.why: LABEL CORRECTED in hardening round 2: MLV703 is not a built rule - it carries the status **later** in docs/ISSUE_RULES.md section 1 - so a label for it can never be satisfied and can never be violated. `analyzer/tests/accuracy/test_accuracy.py::test_every_labelled_code_is_a_real_rule` rejects one, and this row turned that shipped test red. The observation is kept verbatim here so the row can be restored the day the rule ships. Original verdict `forbidden`, original note: THE TRAP: F.dropout at line 41 passes training=self.training explicitly
